text:
leah (release lead): deploy-bot just flagged a canary regression for routing-service v1.14.0 — p95 latency and a few 504s. change window in ~25m.
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary rollout routing-service v1.14.0 p95>threshold (thr=180ms, obs=320ms). Auto-rollback eligible.
omar (sre): seeing transient 504s from edge-proxy when payloads >16k. traces show retry storms and increased connection churn.
jia (eng): recent change in 1.14.0: backpressure tweak + connection pooling adjustments. suspect pool sizing too small under heavy bursts.
dom (pm): are any dedicated customers pinned? blast radius?
ops-oncall: no dedicated pins. canary is ~6% traffic in us-west-2. EU unaffected.
omar (sre): auto-rollback would be fastest, but i want to collect a few full traces to confirm cause. manual pin keeps the canary on older version and preserves traces.
jia (eng): +1 for manual pin. i can push a small config patch to increase pool size and test in staging.
leah (release lead): options: auto-rollback OR manual pin to 1.13.7 then patch. which do we pick?
deploy-bot: USAGE: /deploy rollback --service=routing-service --to=1.13.7 --scope=canary OR /deploy pin-version --service=routing-service --version=1.13.7 --scope=canary --note="p95 spike: connection pooling"
dom (pm): i'll draft a concise customer blurb pre-approved for release after 15m stable.
omar (sre): executing pin now.
omar (sre): /bin/deployctl pin-version --service routing-service --version 1.13.7 --scope canary --note "p95 spike: pool sizing"
omar (sre): pin complete, canary shifted. running 10m smoke + long-payload synthetic.
omar (sre): smoke looks good, p95 returning to baseline. no new 504s. :white_check_mark: 
jia (eng): opened PR: bump-pool-size (https://git.redwood/repo/pull/1001). added load test for >16k payloads.
ops-oncall: holding wider rollout until patch validated. scheduling re-deploy tomorrow 07:00 UTC.
leah (release lead): add note to release changelog: manual pin executed to preserve telemetry and allow root cause triage. dom, post customer blurb once 15m stable.
dom (pm): posted to #customer-briefing: "We observed a regression in a small canary during today's rollout and contained it by rolling the canary back while engineers investigate. No customer action required"
omar (sre): 15m stable, metrics steady. closing this thread, will unpin after staging patch validated.
leah (release lead): thanks all.
